clue.text: Richest part of 25

definitions.meaning: the wealthiest woman, one worth more than a million
the title role of a play by the dramatist at 25-down

explanation.walkthrough: 25-down is SHAW, and The Millionairess (1936) is one of George Bernard Shaw's plays, so the word is both a very rich woman and a role in his work.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman worth over a million is about as rich as anyone, and she is the heroine of a Shaw comedy.

clue.text: Debutantes' addresses?

parts.note: debutantes are newcomers, and an address is a formal talk, so these are the first talks given by new members, as by new MPs in Parliament

explanation.surface: Society girls coming out, and where they live or what they say.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'maiden' is a first of its kind, and a new MP's first speech in the House of Commons has this name; the surface reads debutantes as society girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Debutantes are first-timers, and the first formal talk anyone gives to a body such as Parliament carries this name.

clue.text: Ship engineers love to take over

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something over turns it upside down, so the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
love is nil, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Engineers fond of commandeering a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take over' turns RE + NIL, which reads RENIL, upside down to give the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean-going passenger vessel on a regular route is called by this name.

clue.text: Rising pressure to support party in power

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the pressure word comes after the party

parts.note: the 'ins' are the party in office, as opposed to the outs
urgency is pressure, as of time or need

explanation.surface: Pressure building up to prop up the governing party.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to support' puts URGENCY under INS. 'Rising' is a noun here: a revolt, not getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is a revolt against authority, the same as an insurrection.

clue.text: Sort of slopes where trees are from grown

definitions.meaning: gentle ski runs for beginners take this name
a plot where young plants and trees are raised from seed

explanation.walkthrough: The word order 'are from grown' is as printed; it means 'are grown from'. Nursery slopes are the easy ski runs where beginners learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginners' ski runs are named after a children's room, and a plant-raising place has the same name, both sharing the idea of early growth.

clue.text: Rough location of repealed legislation

parts.note: in is the word that tells where something is
ex means former, no longer in force
an act is a piece of legislation passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: Where a law that has been struck off can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'in ex-act': where a repealed law would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is not precise, so rough means lacking accuracy.

clue.text: Test team drops opener unnamed character's included

indicators.note: the unnamed character is put inside what is left of team
the word team loses its first letter, its opener

parts.note: X stands for an unknown or unnamed person, as in Mr X

explanation.surface: In a cricket Test, a side loses its opening batsman and brings in a mystery player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops opener' takes the T off TEAM to leave EAM, and 'included' puts X inside it. The surface talks about cricket: a Test is an international match and the opener is the first batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is an examination, a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Canvas spread, in turn, over drum

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to spin is to turn round
a naker is an old kettledrum

explanation.surface: A tent canvas thrown over a drum while turning.
explanation.walkthrough: A naker is a medieval kettledrum, a word now found mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A large triangular sail spread before the wind on a yacht is made of canvas or sailcloth.

clue.text: Steady profit herbalist has

definitions.meaning: return on money calculated only on the original sum, earning the same each period
medicinal herbs are called simples, so a herbalist is concerned with them

explanation.walkthrough: Old herbal remedies of a single plant are called 'simples', so a herbalist has an interest in simples.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest paid only on the principal gives a steady, unchanging return, and a herb doctor cares about medicinal plants.

clue.text: Good news for travellers in poetic island

definitions.meaning: a vacant room at a hostelry
the lake isle in Yeats's poem 'The Lake Isle of' this name

explanation.walkthrough: W B Yeats wrote 'I will arise and go now, and go to' this Irish island; split up it says an inn has room.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeats's poem names this island in Lough Gill, and a travellers' hostelry with vacancies is welcome news.

clue.text: Defence of party member's self disclosure

parts.note: a party member could be a Lib, a member of the Liberal Party
I is how a speaker refers to themself

explanation.surface: A politician pleading his case with a confession about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: A Liberal saying 'a Lib, I' discloses himself. 'Defence' is the plea in court that one was elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that the accused was elsewhere when the crime happened is a defence in law.

clue.text: Point to nothing in basic education that's wrong

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

indicators.note: the nothing goes inside the letters for basic education

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A teacher pointing out a failing in the fundamentals of schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic, so basic education gives RRR, and O goes in between the second and third R.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or misdeed is a wrong, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Times editor avoids selecting extreme letters

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of each of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: The editor of The Times steers clear of choosing headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'selecting extreme letters' takes the first and last letters of 'editor' and 'avoids'. 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are long periods of history, which are also called times.

clue.text: Cut tail off bird

indicators.note: the last letter of the bird's name is removed

parts.note: a snipe is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: Docking a bird's tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail off' takes the E from the end of SNIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors.

clue.text: Odd things to say when retiring

definitions.text: Odd things to say when retiring

parts.words: Odd things to say when retiring
parts.note: a childish goodnight said on going to bed, which is a doubled word, and said as you retire for the evening rather than at night's start

explanation.surface: Strange remarks people make on leaving their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' means going to bed, not leaving work; the goodnight wish repeats one word, which makes it odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy way of saying goodnight on going to bed repeats one word, which is the oddity the clue points to.

clue.text: He plays remarkably, being in good form

indicators.note: doing something remarkably suggests an unusual arrangement, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician on top form playing outstandingly well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' rearranges HE PLAYS. 'In good form' sounds like playing well but means having a nice figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with an attractive figure is well proportioned, which is to have a good form.

clue.text: In pursuit of news? A novel conclusion

parts.note: to be after something is to chase it
word is news, as in 'any word from them?'

explanation.surface: A reporter chasing a story reaches an unusual ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new' but is the noun: a book's closing section.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing section added at the end of a book is its last word, a conclusion to a novel.

clue.text: Gleam in the eye of Tupman's capital fellow-member

indicators.note: a capital letter is a word's first, so only the opening letter of the name is used

parts.note: Nathaniel Winkle is, with Tupman, a member of the Pickwick Club in Dickens's novel

explanation.surface: A sparkle in the eye of a fellow clubman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's The Pickwick Papers, Tracy Tupman and Nathaniel Winkle are fellow members of the Pickwick Club; the capital of Tupman is T.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinkle is a bright glint or sparkle in someone's eyes.

clue.text: Offers incentive to enter apprenticeship

indicators.note: the answer is found by going inside the letters of the last word

explanation.surface: Inducements offered to take up an apprenticeship.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in 'apprENTICESHip'; 'enter' tells you to look inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt with an inducement, so offering incentive is exactly that.

clue.text: Warriors showing spirit, turning up in parts of Asia

indicators.note: the reversed spirit goes inside the rearranged letters
the letters of the continent's name are broken into parts and rearranged
in a down clue turning up reads the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a distilled drink

explanation.surface: Fighters showing courage turn up in parts of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses RUM to MUR; 'parts of' breaks up ASIA into SA..AI, and 'in' puts MUR in the middle. 'Spirit' looks like courage but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan.

clue.text: One who suffers pain, on its woeful waters

parts.note: someone who aches is an acher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sufferer going on about its sorrowful waters.
explanation.walkthrough: Acheron, river of woe, is one of the rivers of the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this underworld river's name means 'river of woe', so its waters are sorrowful.

clue.text: Number to object in foreign Parliament

indicators.note: the number is put inside the words for object

parts.note: an object is a thing
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A deputy rising to object in a parliament abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L, Roman fifty, inside A THING. The Althing is the parliament of Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland's national assembly, one of the oldest parliaments, is a legislature overseas from Britain.

clue.text: Bennett's character gets out of hand in play

definitions.meaning: Denry Machin, hero of Arnold Bennett's novel The ..., is a cheeky, clever fellow

definitions.text: gets out of hand in play
definitions.meaning: in a ... game a player's piece leaves the hand when played

explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Bennett's 1911 novel The Card is about a likeable rogue; a 'card' is also a joker of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Bennett's comic hero is a lively character, and in a game the pasteboard leaves one's hand when played.

clue.text: Great physician's turn give off thus

indicators.note: turning the word round makes it read backwards

parts.note: the proverb says time is the great healer, or great physician

explanation.surface: A celebrated doctor's turn to give off heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is the great physician' is an old proverb (Disraeli used it); 'turn' reverses TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, as a light gives off rays.

clue.text: In reformed church, note place for statue

indicators.note: something reformed is remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: In a Protestant church, take note of where the statue stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' looks like the Reformation but rearranges IN to NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess in a wall built to hold a statue or ornament is a niche.

clue.text: Car for two people, but no inexperienced driver

indicators.note: the inexperienced driver is taken away from the pair

parts.note: a couple is two people
L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A two-seater car, but not for a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display an L plate, so L stands for an inexperienced driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupe is a closed two-door car, often seating two.

clue.text: Second thorn-tree in thicket

parts.note: the haw is the hawthorn, and its berry

explanation.surface: A second thorn bush within a thicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaw' is an old word for a small wood or thicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaw is a small wood or copse, an old dialect word for a thicket.

clue.text: Date hard to manage? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to read the wordplay the opposite way round, from end to start

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: A romantic engagement that is difficult to handle, or quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' turns H + COPE, read HCOPE, back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a point or period of time from which events are dated.

clue.text: Again urge changes in measure for fall

indicators.note: the word says the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone presses for changes once more in a falling measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges AGAIN URGE. 'Fall' is rainfall, not autumn or a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures how much rain has fallen.

clue.text: College, by the way, houses VIPs

parts.note: Downing is a college of Cambridge University
a street is a way, a road

explanation.surface: A college by the road accommodates important people.
explanation.walkthrough: Downing College is in Cambridge; Downing Street in London holds the homes of the Prime Minister and Chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: This London street is the home and office of the Prime Minister and the Chancellor, so it houses top people.
